# Alchemist

> Multi-tenant video transcoding and delivery. Upload or import a video, get an
> adaptive-bitrate stream and a signed playback URL. Self-hosted: Go,
> PostgreSQL, River, SeaweedFS, ffmpeg, shaka-packager. Built Bangladesh-first.

Consumers integrate through the HTTP API with an API key. There is no shared
database, no direct object-storage access, and no internal endpoints. If something
you need is not in the API, that is a gap in the API.

Things that will otherwise surprise you:

- **`partially_ready` means playable.** Ingest encodes a low ladder (144p-360p) and
  returns immediately; 480p and above are generated on first playback. Treat
  `ready` and `partially_ready` as equally playable. Waiting for `ready` will hang
  for content nobody has watched yet.
- **A live stream is an asset.** `live` means a broadcast is happening and playable
  now; `live_ended` means it has finished and its recording is being turned into an
  ordinary video. That conversion needs no re-upload and the asset keeps its id, so a
  link handed out before the broadcast plays the broadcast, then the recording, with
  no gap and nothing to re-fetch. When it lands the asset reaches `ready` or
  `partially_ready` like any upload and `asset.ready` fires.
- **Playback URLs expire** (4h) and carry `exp`, `kid` and `sig`. One signature
  authorizes the manifest, every segment, the content key, the poster and the
  thumbnails. Re-fetch the asset to get a fresh set; do not construct them yourself.
- **Links can be bound to one viewer.** `GET /v1/assets/{id}?viewer=<your-id>&watermark=<label>`
  adds `vid` and `wm` to the URLs, both inside the signature so neither can be edited
  out. The viewer id is yours and stays opaque to us — signed, echoed, never stored.
  `watermark` is a short label your player draws on screen; there is no server-side
  burn-in. Set `max_viewer_devices` (`PUT /v1/playback-settings`, 0-20, 0 means no
  cap) and a bound viewer streaming from more devices than that gets
  `403 viewer_limit_reached` on the newest one. This is the answer to one login shared
  with a class; encryption is not.
- **Errors are `{"error":{"code","message"}}`.** Branch on `code`, which is stable.
  `message` is written for a human and is translated when the request sends
  `Accept-Language: bn`.
- **Media is encrypted by default** for new accounts: `cenc`, with the key endpoint
  answering an EME Clear Key licence (`{"keys":[{"kty":"oct","kid":"...","k":"..."}],
  "type":"temporary"}`, unpadded base64url). Chrome, Firefox and Edge play it with no
  licence vendor. **Safari and iOS cannot** — WebKit's only key system is FairPlay —
  and they get `403 browser_not_supported` from the key endpoint rather than a black
  screen. This is encryption at rest, not DRM: the key reaches the browser in the
  clear behind the signed URL, so a lifted bucket is useless but an entitled viewer
  can still keep a copy. Turn it off per account with `PUT /v1/playback-settings`.
  Existing accounts keep the setting they have, and published videos keep whatever
  they were packaged with.
- **Play whichever URL `playback.preferred` names.** HLS for a clear asset, DASH for
  an encrypted one: encrypted media is packaged `cenc`, and HLS has no `cenc`. Both
  URLs are always returned. DASH is produced too, but only HLS is verified
  end to end.
- **Uploads never pass through the API.** `POST /v1/uploads` returns a presigned
  target; `PUT` the bytes there, then call `/complete`.

## API

- [OpenAPI specification](api/openapi.yaml): Every endpoint, checked against the
  running router by a test in both directions, so it cannot drift.
- [Customer journey script](test/journey.sh): A runnable end-to-end integration
  using only the public API and an API key. The clearest worked example.
- [Customer stand-ins](test/customer_servers.py): A source origin and webhook
  receiver for testing an integration locally.

## Integration flow

```
POST /admin/tenants            -> tenant_id          (operator, admin key)
POST /admin/tenants/{id}/keys  -> api_key            (shown once)

POST /v1/auth/signup           -> tenant + owner + first api_key, in one transaction
POST /v1/auth/login            -> session cookie     (browser, not machine)
POST /v1/auth/logout           -> revokes the session
GET  /v1/auth/session          -> who the cookie belongs to
GET  /v1/auth/invite?token=    -> who a pending invite is for (no account yet)
POST /v1/auth/invite           -> redeem it: account inside an existing tenant + session

POST /v1/uploads               -> presigned upload target + asset_id
PUT  <upload_url>              -> the bytes, direct to storage
POST /v1/assets/{id}/complete  -> queues processing
  or
POST /v1/assets {"url":"..."}  -> import from a URL instead

GET  /v1/assets                -> recent assets, newest first (dashboard listing)
GET  /v1/assets/{id}           -> state, renditions with chunk progress, playback URLs
                                  ?viewer=&watermark= binds the links to one person
GET  /v1/assets/{id}/chunks    -> the chunk map, per rendition
GET  /v1/assets/{id}/activity  -> pipeline steps, states and timings (no error text)
GET  /v1/keys                  -> names and dates, never the key
POST /v1/keys                  -> another key (shown once)
POST /v1/contact               -> an enquiry from the public site (no account)
DELETE /v1/assets/{id}         -> delete a video; media shared with a deduplicated
                                  copy survives until the last of them is gone
DELETE /v1/keys/{id}           -> revoke
POST /v1/webhooks              -> asset.ready, asset.failed, rendition.ready,
                                  live.started, live.ended, live.failed
GET  /v1/usage                 -> billable aggregates: ingest seconds, egress bytes,
                                  storage gb_hours
GET  /v1/branding              -> account name and logo URL
GET  /v1/playback-settings     -> playback encryption, and the per-viewer device cap

Live, present only where this deployment configures ingest, and only for a tenant
who has bought it -- otherwise every endpoint here answers `live_not_enabled` (403).
Live is a separate product from the VOD engine; a customer may hold either or both:
POST   /v1/live-streams           -> create; the stream key is shown once
GET    /v1/live-streams           -> your streams
GET    /v1/live-streams/{id}      -> state and the asset the broadcast plays at
POST   /v1/live-streams/{id}/start -> go on air; returns the ingest_url for OBS
POST   /v1/live-streams/{id}/key  -> replace the stream key; the old one stops working
DELETE /v1/live-streams/{id}      -> delete

live.started fires when the encoder connects, live.ended when the broadcast stops,
live.failed when it never started or the ingest broke (with an error_code). The
recording is reported by asset.ready on the same asset id, so an integrator who
already handles uploads gets the VOD for free.

Session only (an API key gets 403 session_required):
GET    /v1/members             -> teammates and pending invites
POST   /v1/members/invites     -> invite someone; token returned once
DELETE /v1/members/invites/{id}-> withdraw a pending invite
PATCH  /v1/members/{id}        -> change a role
DELETE /v1/members/{id}        -> remove someone (their sessions cascade)
PUT    /v1/playback-settings   -> encryption on/off, and max_viewer_devices (0-20)
PUT    /v1/branding/logo       -> raw image bytes, <=1 MB, png/jpeg/webp
DELETE /v1/branding/logo       -> remove it

GET  /brand/{tenant}/logo      -> the logo, unauthenticated (viewers have no account)
```

The auth endpoints exist for the sign-up page, not for integrations: a session is a
browser thing. Server-to-server code uses the API key from signup and never touches
them. `/v1` accepts either credential — an API key, or that session cookie when the
request comes from a configured browser origin, which is what the customer dashboard
uses so a key never has to live in page script. They are mounted only when `ALCHEMIST_WEB_ORIGINS` names a browser origin, so
a deployment that has no web front end has no account surface at all.

Account administration is session-only by design. An API key is something a server
holds; letting it invite a person or grant a role would turn a leaked key into a
permanent way back into the account. Signup always creates a *new* tenant — redeeming
an invite is the only way a second user joins an existing one. Roles are `owner`,
`admin` and `member`; only an owner can grant ownership, and the last owner can be
neither demoted nor removed.

Invites last seven days and the token is shown once, at creation. There is no mail
sender in this repo yet, so the dashboard displays the link for whoever invited them
to pass on.

Webhook deliveries are signed: `X-Alchemist-Signature: sha256=<hmac of the raw body>`
using the secret returned when the endpoint was registered. Verify it.

## Running it locally

- [Makefile](Makefile): `make db-reset`, `make storage`, `make run`, `make test`.
- [Environment template](.env.example): Every variable is required; the binary
  refuses to start if one is missing, rather than defaulting.
- [Deployment notes](deploy/README.md): Topology, key rotation, and the edge cache.

Requires `ffmpeg`, `packager` (shaka-packager) and `weed` (SeaweedFS) on PATH.
The last two are GitHub release binaries, not in Homebrew.

## Architecture

- [Working conventions and constraints](CLAUDE.md): Non-obvious decisions that were
  established by measurement and are expensive to rediscover. Read before changing
  encoding, caching or signing.
- [Module boundaries](internal/modules/README.md): How the modular monolith is
  separated, and how to extract a module into its own service.

## Optional

- [Edge cache configuration](deploy/edge/nginx.conf): nginx with byte-range slice
  caching. Authorization must run before the cache lookup; the comment there
  explains why.
- [Edge signature validation](deploy/edge/playback_auth.js): njs implementation,
  kept byte-identical to the Go one by a test.
